This also unmounts the %1$d other partitions on this drive.

resources.string: Will eject once the transfer is complete.
Ejected. Android may open this drive now. If it does, use Android\'s Eject before you unplug it.
Ejected. You can unplug it. Android may say this drive is corrupted. Don\'t format it.
Eject of %1$s is waiting for a transfer to finish.
OTG Master leaves a drive alone until you tap Scan USB devices.
OTG Master opens a drive as soon as you plug it in. This is the default.
Android gets a few seconds first. OTG Master opens a drive only if Android did not mount it.
USB drive connected. Tap Scan USB devices to open it.
Waiting to see whether Android mounts this USB drive.
Android is using this USB drive. Tap Scan USB devices to open it here instead.
Android is using a USB drive
Eject it in Android first. If OTG Master takes it now, a file Android is writing can be damaged.
No encrypted volume this app can open was found on this device.
Unlocking… This may take a while
No USB drives available to mount.
Report a problem or suggest an improvement
The form opens in your browser. The app sends nothing: you review the details below and submit the form yourself.
The form will be filled in with exactly this
Open the form with these details
Open the form without any details
Not included: your drive\'s volume label, its serial number, and any file or folder names.
No browser available to open the form

When a known device is connected, OTG Master asks for your device lock, then mounts all recognized encrypted drives automatically. Credentials are encrypted with AES-256 in Android Keystore and cannot be extracted without your device lock. A hidden volume, or a volume mounted with hidden volume protection, is never mounted this way.
The saved credentials for %1$s no longer work, so they were cleared. Enter them again to turn Auto mount back on.
Opt out of Auto mount for this device
Protect hidden volume against damage caused by writing to outer volume

The hidden volume is now protected against damage until the outer volume is unmounted.\n\nIf anything tries to save data to the hidden volume area, OTG Master write-protects the entire volume, both the outer and the hidden part, until it is unmounted. Data saved to that area is lost. This can also corrupt the filesystem on the outer volume, which, if repeated, might weaken the plausible deniability of the hidden volume. Avoid writing to the hidden volume area.

Data was about to be saved to the hidden volume area of %1$s. OTG Master refused it to protect the hidden volume, and that data is lost. This may have corrupted the filesystem on the outer volume.

The entire volume, both the outer and the hidden part, is write-protected until it is unmounted.

If this has happened before on this volume, the plausible deniability of the hidden volume might be affected. Consider creating a new VeraCrypt volume with quick format off, moving your files to it, and securely erasing this one.
%1$s is write-protected until it is unmounted. Open OTG Master for details.
%1$s stopped taking writes until it is unmounted.
Not available for a hidden or protected outer volume
Backups are disabled in Settings. Enable them to back up this drive?
Hides the backup reminder icon, the Backups tab, Manage backups and each drive\'s list of backups. Backups you have already scheduled keep running.
Mount encrypted partitions read-only by default
All Auto mount cached credentials cleared.
USB permission not granted for %1$s (answered after %2$d s: Deny, or the prompt was dismissed). Tap Scan USB devices to be asked again.
%1$s was unplugged %2$d s after USB permission was asked for, before it was answered.
%1$s disconnected while mounted. If it drops during transfers, it may need more power than the phone can supply. Try a powered USB hub or an enclosure with its own power supply.
%1$s disconnected while mounted. Check the cable and connections.

The phone was on battery when this drive dropped. The most common cause is power: SSDs and hard drives in bus-powered enclosures can draw more than a phone\'s USB port supplies, especially during long transfers.
The phone was on external power when this drive dropped, so a weak power supply is less likely. Start with the connection.
Use a USB hub with its own power supply: plug the hub into the wall, the drive into the hub, and the hub into the phone.
Or use an enclosure with its own power input.
Use a short, direct USB-C cable. Avoid loose adapters, and make sure each plug is fully seated.
Keep the phone charged. Some phones limit USB power when the battery is low.

If files were being written when it dropped, check the drive on a computer before writing to it again (chkdsk on Windows, fsck.exfat or e2fsck on Linux). An ext4 drive may open read-only until its journal is repaired, which its card offers. Reading it is safe.
Plug the drive back in to mount it again. Its disconnects stay listed on its card until the app closes.
Unplug the drive and plug it back in. When Android asks whether OTG Master may access it, tap Allow.
Connect it with an OTG adapter, or a USB-C drive directly. Some cables only charge and carry no data.
Some phones, including OnePlus, Oppo, Realme and Vivo, read USB drives only while OTG is switched on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"). It switches itself off after a few minutes unused.
Some phones cannot read a drive while charging through the same port. If the drive appears only with the charger unplugged, connect it directly with an OTG adapter.

SSDs and hard drives may need more power than the phone can supply. If the drive\'s light stays off, or it disconnects shortly after appearing, try a USB hub with its own power supply, on a phone that can read drives through one.
Drives locked by their own hardware, such as WD\'s password lock, must be unlocked with the maker\'s software first.
Encryption: VeraCrypt (AES, Serpent, Twofish and their cascades), LUKS1, LUKS2, BitLocker, and encrypted APFS.
File systems: FAT32, exFAT, NTFS and ext4, read and write; APFS, read-only.
Unencrypted drives with these file systems open on their own when plugged in.
Not unmounted cleanly. Read-only until repaired.
This ext4 drive was not unmounted cleanly, so its journal still holds changes that never reached their place on the drive. Until they do, OTG Master opens it read-only.
Repairing replays the journal: it applies those changes, the same way Linux does the next time it mounts the drive. No files are deleted.
If any part of the journal fails its checksum, nothing is changed and the drive stays read-only. Check it on a computer with e2fsck.
%1$s repaired: %2$d journal transaction(s) replayed, %3$d block(s) written. It is writable now.
%1$s was not repaired and stays read-only: %2$s
Drive repaired. It is writable now.
Repair failed. The drive stays read-only. See the log.
The phone is locked or OTG Master is not on screen: USB drives will be opened when it is back on screen, so Android lets OTG Master keep them readable behind other apps.
The background service that keeps drives readable behind other apps is now running.
Notifications allowed: mounted drives, Format and Encrypt progress and backup reminders will show in the notification shade.
The notifications question was closed without an answer; asking again.
Allow notification permission for OTG Master to keep drives open for other apps.
Helps keep Android from closing mounted drives while other apps use them.\n\nShows backup, format and encrypt progress, and reminders.
Opened OTG Master\'s notification settings; the drive mounts when you come back.

Notifications are off for OTG Master: drives still mount and stay readable behind other apps, but the mounted-drive notice, Format and Encrypt progress and backup reminders will not show. Turn them on in Android Settings › Apps › OTG Master › Notifications.
Tap to open it in OTG Master.

%1$s was plugged in and Android did not open OTG Master for it (another app is the default, or the phone was locked with no default set); a notification offers to open it. Choosing OTG Master with \"Always\" opens it directly next time.
%1$s was plugged in and Android did not open OTG Master for it; notifications are off, so OTG Master could not offer to open it.
%1$d locked partition(s) on %2$s, beside one already mounted.
Found %1$d VeraCrypt volume candidates on QEMU disk.
This phone does not support USB drives (it reports no USB host / OTG support).
This phone\'s USB port is connected to a computer, with the phone as the device, so it cannot read a drive through that port.

This phone is charging through its USB port. Many phones cannot read USB drives while charging that way: if the drive is on a hub with a power supply, unplug the power supply, or connect the drive directly with an OTG adapter.
OTG connection is switched off, so USB drives cannot be seen. Turn it on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"), then plug the drive in again.
On %1$s phones, USB drives work only while OTG is switched on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"). It switches itself off after a few minutes unused.
Still waiting for USB permission for %1$s (asked %2$d s ago): tap Allow on Android\'s prompt; if none is showing, unplug and replug the drive.
Could not open RawBlockDevice via libaums: no USB device to open (all were already open or in use).
Unlock attempt on %1$s: pim=%2$s, cipher=%3$s, hash=%4$s
Cannot mount: %1$s is not yet supported.
Filesystem not recognized. Trying to mount it anyway.
Could not mount this filesystem. Supported: FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, ext4 and APFS.
%1$s is not encrypted: it holds a plain %2$s filesystem, so there is nothing to unlock.
Could not open files app directly: %1$s
Drives you unlock or plug in appear here.
Every sector is overwritten. Slower: about a minute per GB over USB.
Only the filesystem structures are written. The old data stays on the drive, readable with recovery tools, until it is overwritten.
Keep the drive attached and the app open until this finishes.
Everything on this partition will be erased.
The new volume stays inside its encrypted container, with the same password, and keeps the partition\'s size. The same filesystem also keeps its cluster size.
The partition keeps its size. The same filesystem also keeps its cluster size.
This erases the partition and creates a new, empty encrypted volume on it. Your current files are not moved into it: copy them somewhere else first.
The PIM must be a number.
With a password under %2$d characters, the PIM must be at least %1$d, or empty.
Too short for this PIM. Use at least %1$d characters, or change the PIM.
VeraCrypt passwords are at most %1$d bytes.
Save the password in my password manager
Password saved in your password manager as \"%1$s\".
The password was not saved in your password manager (%1$s).
Empty for VeraCrypt\'s default (416 MiB, 6 passes). Higher values need more memory and time to unlock.

LUKS2 is Linux\'s own encryption: AES-256 in XTS mode, the password protected by Argon2id. Linux desktops open it with the password; Windows and macOS need extra software. For a drive used on Windows or a Mac too, choose VeraCrypt.
Keep a copy of every keyfile: the volume cannot be opened without them. Their order does not matter.
Up to %1$d characters. Clear it for no label.
All data on %1$s (%2$s) will be cleared. This cannot be undone.
Encrypted (%1$s, %2$s) with %3$s inside. Unlock it now with the password, PIM and keyfiles you chose, to check they open it before you copy anything onto it.
Keep the drive attached until it finishes
Files stay available in other apps until you unmount.
Open OTG Master to run it now.
%1$s hasn\'t been backed up in a while
Connect %1$s to back up your files now.
%1$s is ready to run. It may slow other transfers on this drive.
Waiting for another backup to finish
Part of this backup is damaged, so it can\'t be trusted. Recreate it from the source to get a good backup. The damaged backup stays on the drive in a folder of its own until you delete it.
Open OTG Master to recreate it from the source.
The reminder and its history are removed from this phone. The copies on the drive stay.
Set a screen lock to view this password.
Enter the password to continue backups
This phone doesn\'t have the password for %1$s. It is checked against the backup before it is saved.
This phone can no longer open a folder this backup uses.
This folder is itself a restic backup. Choose a folder outside it.
This folder belongs to the backup %1$s. Choose a folder outside it.
The backup %1$s already uses this folder. Choose another target or name.
The folder %1$s holds a restic backup, so a Plain backup can\'t go there. Choose Incremental to continue that backup, or use another name.
The folder %1$s holds a restic backup that this password doesn\'t open.
This drive is mounted read-only: it can be the source, not the target.
The source and the target are the same folder.
The backup goes into a folder of this name in the target.
A full copy in a dated folder each time.
Snapshots: only what changed is stored again. Encrypted with a password.

Every backup is a complete copy of the files in a folder named by its date. Any computer or phone reads them with no app and no password. Each backup takes the full space again, and they are not encrypted: anyone holding the drive can read them.

Every backup is a snapshot of the folder as it was, and files that did not change are not stored again, so many backups take little more space than one. Snapshots are encrypted with the backup\'s password and checked when read. They are kept in the standard restic repository format: this app restores files from them and can mount a backup to browse it, and on a computer the free restic tool (restic.net) opens them with the same password. Without restic or this app, and without the password, the files cannot be read.
Choose a backup folder directly inside %1$s.
Password correct. New backups continue in this backup.
OTG Master sends a reminder at the interval you choose to connect the drive or drives, so you can start the backup.

The password that encrypts these backups. Save it in your password manager: without it nobody, including this app on a new phone, can open them. If this backup\'s folder already holds a restic repository, enter its password instead.
No devices mounted to create a backup reminder
No backups found at this location.
Enter the password of the backup in %1$s.
That password does not open this backup.
Connect and unlock %1$s to mount this backup.
No backups use this drive yet.
The reminder, its history and its saved password are removed from this phone. The backups on the drive stay, but nothing can open them without the password, so save it first.
On a computer: restic -r <drive>/<folder> snapshots, with this password.
Recovery works on FAT32 and exFAT
Looking for deleted files. Nothing is written to the drive.
Only deleted files are listed. They are copied to a folder you choose on the phone or another drive, never to this one, so nothing still recoverable is overwritten.
Scan stopped. Nothing is listed: until every folder is read, a file that was only moved or renamed cannot be told from a deleted one.
Deleted files can no longer be found when their space has been reused, when the drive was formatted since, or, on FAT32, when they were deleted through OTG Master, which removes the entry entirely.
Choose a folder on the phone or on another drive: writing to this one could overwrite the files being recovered.
